_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and x19-rb-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: AIR via airplane and JET via jet plane; both instantly familiar, a clean easy clue (STREAM, via airstream and jet stream, would be a fine alternative).

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean pair; STREAM is a slightly less obvious alternative.

hints.reason: APPLE via 'apple of my eye' and PUPIL as part of the eye, with the true bonus that the phrase originally meant the pupil.

pairs.pair_note: TEACHER (apple for the teacher, a teacher's pupil) would be an equally good double-meaning alternative.

hints.reason: BAG via Mary Poppins's bottomless bag and CARPET via its being a carpetbag; the carpet side takes a beat but clicks once seen.

pairs.pair_note: Nice aha; lines are accurate to the 1964 film.

hints.reason: BATH via the famous eureka-in-the-bath story and CROWN via the gold-crown test that prompted it; the crown detail is less known but is the core of the same story.

pairs.pair_note: Classic science legend; lines correctly framed as legend.

hints.reason: BED and ROCK both via the Flintstones' hometown Bedrock, with flint as a rock as a bonus; a satisfying split-compound.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, fun pair.

hints.reason: BITE via the bitten-apple logo and COMPUTER via Mac computers; universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: BOOT via boot polish and KIWI via the Kiwi shoe-polish brand; the brand is widely sold in the U.S., though some players will think of the fruit first.

pairs.pair_note: Brand link is fair; the kiwi-bird naming line is true.

hints.reason: BREAD via Wonder Bread and SUPERHERO via Wonder Woman; two iconic names, instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good brand-plus-character pairing.

hints.reason: BUFFALO via Buffalo Bill and WILD via Wild Bill Hickok; two famous Old West Bills make a cohesive, satisfying pair.

pairs.pair_note: Thematically unified phrase-join; also echoes the Buffalo Bills.

hints.reason: YODA via his pupil Luke Skywalker and CAGE via Marvel's Luke Cage; Luke Cage is less universal but known from the Netflix series.

pairs.pair_note: Two different Lukes; CAGE side is the softer one.

hints.reason: CAPTAIN via Captain Hook and RIGHT via a right hook punch; both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, easy.

hints.reason: CHAIN via chain links and FENCE via the chain-link fence; the fence side leans on the other target but the compound is very familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; fence route depends on 'chain-link' as a unit.

hints.reason: CHECK via checkmate and SOUL via soulmate; instantly familiar compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Classic compound pair.

hints.reason: CLEAN via scrub meaning to clean hard and NURSE via the scrubs nurses wear; a true double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning; synonym note only.

hints.reason: RING via the mood ring and COLOR via its colour changes; a familiar, coherent single-object link.

pairs.pair_note: Lines correctly attribute the change to temperature.

hints.reason: CRASH via Wedding Crashers / crashing a wedding and PARTY via the wedding party; both familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fair, mild delight.

hints.reason: DINOSAUR via museum dinosaur skeletons and HISTORY via the natural history museum; straightforward and true.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but honest.

hints.reason: DRESS via the ball gown and PUMPKIN via the pumpkin coach, both from the fairy godmother scene.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, iconic.

hints.reason: EARTH via Earth's crust and THIN via thin-crust pizza; a neat science-meets-food double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning, and Earth's crust really is thin relative to the planet.

hints.reason: FALL via acorns falling (and autumn) and SKY via Chicken Little, whom a falling acorn convinces the sky is falling; a real aha chain, though the acorn detail may not come to every player unprompted.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: the acorn is a well-known story detail (picture books, Disney 2005), but a player could pair FALL with a tree word instead; CHICKEN would be the safer, flatter alternative.

hints.reason: FATHER via the priest's title and GOD via the priest's service to God; honest on both sides if unremarkable.

pairs.pair_note: A Godfather split (CORLEONE) would add more delight, like Flintstones/Bedrock, but PRIEST is fair.

hints.reason: FLASH via a lightning bolt's flash (and the Flash's lightning-bolt emblem) and THUNDER via thunderbolt; clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: LIGHTNING is the obvious alternative; BOLT is equally fair and slightly less on-the-nose.

hints.reason: TIGER via Tony the Tiger and FROST via the Frosted Flakes he fronts; a classic cereal-mascot aha.

pairs.pair_note: Fun and broadly known.

hints.reason: GATE via the Golden Gate and TICKET via Wonka's golden ticket; two iconic references, instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Strong phrase-join; lines accurate.

hints.reason: GOLF via the putt stroke and SINK via 'sink a putt'; familiar golf idiom.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and clean; SINK's kitchen sense is a nice misdirect.

hints.reason: HARD and ROCK only as the first two words of Hard Rock Cafe, so the hint points at the targets' own phrase rather than each word; DIAMOND (the hardest natural material, slang 'rock') would be a clearly better double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: The name is famous but the link is a positional phrase-join with flat lines; prefer DIAMOND.

hints.reason: HOOD via Robin Hood and SUPERHERO via Batman's partner Robin; two famous Robins.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, fun.

hints.reason: SOFT via 'soft serve' and ICE CREAM because soft serve is ice cream; instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; SERVE's tennis sense adds mild misdirection.

hints.reason: JAPAN via sake as its traditional drink and RICE as what sake is brewed from; true and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: SUSHI would also work; SAKE is fine.

hints.reason: LADY via Lady Justice and SCALE via the scales she holds (the scales of justice); familiar imagery.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; lines accurate.

hints.reason: LONDON via the Tube nickname for its Underground and VACUUM via the vacuum tube; a crisp double meaning most U.S. players know.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: MILK via 'crying over spilled milk' and TEA via 'spill the tea' gossip slang; two familiar idioms on two drinks.

pairs.pair_note: Lively pairing of an old saying and modern slang.

hints.reason: NEW via fresh as a synonym and PRINCE via The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air; the synonym plus a strong pop-culture second side works well.

pairs.pair_note: Good; synonym note only.

hints.reason: OIL via the gushing crude and WELL because a gusher is an uncontrolled oil well; one concept covering the targets' own phrase, but fair.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the term is familiar from Western oil-boom imagery.

hints.reason: PASS via passing the baton in a relay race (and relay meaning to pass along) and TORCH via the Olympic torch relay; also evokes 'pass the torch'.

pairs.pair_note: Fair, coherent.

hints.reason: SWITCH via the Nintendo Switch and POKEMON via its Nintendo games; direct, if not surprising.

pairs.pair_note: Direct; could note Nintendo co-owns Pokémon, but the lines are true as written.

hints.reason: RACE and TURTLE both via the Tortoise and the Hare fable; tortoises are turtles, so the line is accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, easy.

hints.reason: SAIL via wind filling a sail and SURFING via windsurfing; clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy.

hints.reason: SHIELD via a spacecraft heat shield and WAVE via a heat wave; both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Clean phrase-join.

hints.reason: SPONGEBOB via his friend Sandy Cheeks and SQUIRREL because Sandy is a squirrel; widely known cartoon character.

pairs.pair_note: Lines accurate (karate, treedome).

hints.reason: SWEET via sweetheart and VALENTINE via the heart symbol; also evokes Sweethearts candy hearts.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, satisfying.

hints.reason: TRAIN via steam trains and WHISTLE via the steam whistle; fair, if unsurprising.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but sound.
